chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: O people!

Verily Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) to you and revealed the Book to him with the Truth, while you were illiterate regarding the Book and the One Who revealed it, and regarding the Messenger and the One Who sent him — at a time of a gap in messengership, and a prolonged slumber among the nations, and a spreading of ignorance, and the prevalence of strife, and the breaking of solemn covenants, and blindness from the Truth, and oppression by tyrants, and the obliteration of religion, and the blazing of wars — at a time of yellowing of the orchards of the gardens of this world, and the drying of their branches, and the scattering of their leaves, and despair from their fruits, and the drying up of their waters.

The banners of guidance had decayed and the banners of destruction had appeared. The world was scowling in the faces of its inhabitants, gloomy and turning away without facing. Its fruit was strife, its food was carrion, its slogan was fear, and its garment was the sword — you were torn apart entirely. It had blinded the eyes of its inhabitants and darkened their days. They had severed their family ties, shed each other's blood, and buried alive their female infants among their own children. Comfort and the welfare of low worldly life passed them by. They neither hoped for reward from God nor feared, by God, His punishment. Their living were blind and filthy, and their dead were in the Fire in utter despair.

Then he (the Messenger) came to them with a copy of what was in the former Scriptures, and a confirmation of what was before him, and a detailed explanation of the permissible from the doubtful of the forbidden. That is the Quran. So try to make it speak, but it will never speak to you. I will inform you about it: in it is knowledge of what has passed and knowledge of what is to come until the Day of Judgment, and a ruling for what is between you, and an explanation of that about which you have come to dispute. So if you were to ask me about it, I would teach you.

key_terms.أُمِّيُّونَ: Illiterates — those unacquainted with revealed scripture
key_terms.الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَى: The former Scriptures — referring to the scrolls of Abraham and Moses
key_terms.الْمَوْءُودَة: The girl buried alive — referring to the pre-Islamic practice of female infanticide
key_terms.فَاسْتَنْطِقُوهُ: Try to make it speak — address the Quran with questions (it will not answer; the Imam will)
key_terms.فَتْرَة: Gap in prophethood — the period between Jesus and Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the state of pre-Islamic Arabia and the Quran in this sermon?
ai.summary: This is a portion of a famous khutba (sermon) of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), preserved through Imam al-Sadiq (AS). In vivid rhetorical imagery, the Imam describes the state of pre-Islamic Arabian society — marked by ignorance, tribalism, oppression, infanticide, and spiritual blindness — to establish the necessity and magnitude of the Prophet's mission. The sermon then shifts to exalt the Quran as the comprehensive repository of all knowledge, explicitly claiming that Imam Ali himself possesses the key to its interpretation — a cornerstone of Shia doctrine regarding the Imam's authoritative knowledge of the Book.
